root_cause.text: The i915 VRR enable sequence programmed transcoder VRR timing registers in the wrong order, writing TRANS_VRR_VMAX/FLIPLINE before the display transcoder’s TRANS_DDI_FUNC_CTL was enabled, which can hang ICL hardware.
root_cause.evidence: The patch removes `intel_vrr_set_transcoder_timings(crtc_state);` from `hsw_configure_cpu_transcoder()`, adds it later in `intel_vrr_transcoder_enable()`, and adds a `drm_WARN_ON()` explicitly checking `TRANS_DDI_FUNC_ENABLE` before VRR timing writes; the commit message states “ICL may hang with an MCE if we write TRANS_VRR_VMAX/FLIPLINE before enabling TRANS_DDI_FUNC_CTL” and that BSpec requires VRR to be programmed after `TRANS_DDI_FUNC_CTL`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove VRR transcoder timing programming from Haswell CPU transcoder configuration to avoid applying incorrect or duplicate timing updates in this path.
intent_record.what: The call to intel_vrr_set_transcoder_timings(crtc_state); was removed from hsw_configure_cpu_transcoder() immediately after intel_set_transcoder_timings(crtc_state).
intent_record.how: At runtime, this function no longer applies VRR-specific transcoder timing programming during Haswell CPU transcoder configuration, leaving only the standard transcoder timing setup in this path and preventing redundant or incorrect VRR timing updates from occurring here.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a warning guard to catch VRR timing programming before TRANS_DDI_FUNC_CTL is enabled, helping detect an ordering issue that can hang ICL.
intent_record.what: A new warning check and explanatory comment block were added near the start of intel_vrr_set_transcoder_timings(). The code now calls drm_WARN_ON(display->drm, !(intel_de_read(display, TRANS_DDI_FUNC_CTL(display, cpu_transcoder)) & TRANS_DDI_FUNC_ENABLE)); before programming VRR-related registers, after the existing HAS_VRR(display) early return.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this adds a diagnostic warning if the function is reached before TRANS_DDI_FUNC_CTL has been enabled for the transcoder. It does not stop execution, but it helps detect and flag an invalid register programming order that can cause hangs on ICL when TRANS_VRR_VMAX/FLIPLINE are written too early.

intent_record.intent_summary: Set transcoder timings before the VRR capability check so timing configuration is applied even when VRR enable exits early.
intent_record.what: A new call to intel_vrr_set_transcoder_timings(crtc_state); was inserted at the start of intel_vrr_transcoder_enable() before the existing intel_vrr_possible(crtc_state) check and early return.
intent_record.how: This makes the function program or update VRR-related transcoder timings whenever intel_vrr_transcoder_enable() runs, even in cases where VRR is later deemed not possible and the function returns early. It ensures transcoder timing state is initialized or corrected before the capability check.

Since the root cause is improper ordering of VRR timing register writes relative to enabling TRANS_DDI_FUNC_CTL, this is directly related to preventing the problematic VRR timing programming sequence.

The change directly targets the root cause by detecting the unsafe ordering of VRR timing register programming before TRANS_DDI_FUNC_CTL is enabled, which is exactly the sequence that can hang ICL hardware.

    drm/i915/vrr: Move HAS_VRR() check into intel_vrr_set_transcoder_timings()

    the HAS_VRR() check into intel_vrr_set_transcoder_timings().

bic_trace_step.reason: The snippet is sufficient because it shows the ordering of the relevant calls inside the transcoder enable/configure path. The vulnerable root cause is that VRR timing registers are programmed before the transcoder is enabled via TRANS_DDI_FUNC_CTL/related enable sequencing. In this function, `intel_vrr_set_transcoder_timings(crtc_state);` is called at line 1584, before `hsw_set_transconf(crtc_state);` at line 1592. The root-cause description says programming VRR timing registers too early can hang ICL hardware. There is no indication here of any deferral or guard that would move the VRR register programming until after the transcoder enable step. Therefore the vulnerable construct is present (`has_bug=true`) and the fix is not yet present (`is_fixed=false`).

bic_trace_step.reason: The function body is sufficient because it shows the exact ordering of the transcoder programming sequence. The vulnerable construct is present: VRR timing registers are programmed at lines 1636-1637 via `if (HAS_VRR(display)) intel_vrr_set_transcoder_timings(crtc_state);` before the transcoder is enabled at line 1645 via `hsw_set_transconf(crtc_state);`. Per the root cause, writing VRR timing state (`TRANS_VRR_VMAX/FLIPLINE`) before enabling the display transcoder through `TRANS_DDI_FUNC_CTL` can hang ICL hardware. There is no indication of the fix in this function; the fix would require moving VRR timing programming to after the transcoder enable sequence, which has not been done.

bic_trace_step.code_snippet:
commit 99cfbed19d06dfe9c9929c436b5a768231c05b70
Author: Ville Syrjälä <ville.syrjala@linux.intel.com>
Date:   Tue Mar 21 15:56:15 2023 +0200

    drm/i915/vrr: Relocate VRR enable/disable
    
    Move VRR enabling/disabling into a place where it also works
    for fastsets.
    
    With this we always start the transcoder up in non-VRR mode.
    Granted  we already did that but for a very short period of
    time. But now that we might end up doing a bit more with the
    transcoder in non-VRR
bic_trace_step.reason: The diff is sufficient because it shows exactly where VRR timing programming and VRR enable were moved relative to transcoder enable/update paths. The root cause is programming VRR timing registers before the transcoder's DDI function is enabled. This commit changes the sequence so the transcoder is started in non-VRR mode and VRR is enabled later. Specifically, in `intel_enable_crtc()` the code now does `/* VRR will be enable later, if required */ intel_crtc_update_active_timings(new_crtc_state, false);` instead of using `new_crtc_state->vrr.enable`, which means initial bring-up is explicitly non-VRR. In `hsw_configure_cpu_transcoder()` the code programs `intel_set_transcoder_timings(crtc_state);` and then `if (HAS_VRR(dev_priv)) intel_vrr_set_transcoder_timings(crtc_state);`, i.e. VRR timing registers are configured as part of transcoder setup, before actual VRR enable. Actual VRR enable is deferred to `intel_update_crtc()` via `if (vrr_enabling(old_crtc_state, new_crtc_state)) { intel_vrr_enable(new_crtc_state); intel_crtc_update_active_timings(new_crtc_state, new_crtc_state->vrr.enable); }`, which occurs after `crtc_enable()`. This matches the fix described by the root cause: timing registers are no longer being enabled in the hazardous order; the transcoder comes up first without VRR, and VRR is only enabled later. Therefore the vulnerable construct is not present in this commit version, and the fix is already present.
